system_prompt:
You are taking the TIMSS mathematics test for students in the eighth grade. Answer each question as well as you can.

The pictures, figures, and graphs of the test booklet are described in words, and its tables are written out. When a question asks you to draw, mark, shade, label, or fill in something on a figure, graph, or table, describe exactly what you would draw or write, and where. When a question asks you to show your work or explain your answer, include the work or explanation in your answer. For a multiple-choice question, choose one option.
user_prompt:
Using line segment AO below, draw a straight line BC through O such that angle AOB is acute and angle AOC is obtuse. Label points B and C.

[Image: Line segment AO]

Figure, described in words:
A vertical line segment is drawn with a point at the top labeled with the letter "A" above it, and a point at the bottom labeled with the letter "O" below it.

answer.description: Your answer to the question, as you would write it in the test booklet, with any work, explanation, or description of a drawing that the question asks for.
answer.title: Answer

output.answer: Draw a straight line through point O that is not vertical (not along AO), so that it crosses AO only at O. Label one point on the line to the right of O as B, and label one point on the line to the left of O as C, so that B and C lie on opposite sides of O along the line BC. Because the line BC is tilted rather than vertical, angle AOB (between the upward segment OA and the ray OB going up-right) is acute, and angle AOC (between OA and the ray OC going down-left, i.e., on the other side) is obtuse, since angle AOB plus angle AOC equals 180 degrees.
